article_title: Development of a Conceptual Framework for Knowledge Integration in Learning Newton's Third Law
citation: Lei Bao and Joseph C. Fritchman. (2020). Development of a Conceptual Framework for Knowledge Integration in Learning Newton's Third Law. The Ohio State University, Department of Physics. https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1712238
title: Conceptual framework model for Newton's third law built around a central interaction idea
description: The article develops a conceptual framework for Newton's third law in which a central idea serves as a core conceptual node linking basic properties, intermediate reasoning processes, and contextual features. The framework's layers are connected by arrows representing reasoning pathways: solid arrows represent experts' conceptual pathways while dashed-line arrows represent novices' reasoning. It is offered as an operational tool to model students' knowledge structures and inform assessment and instruction.
requirements: The central idea must be identified from expert views, and student difficulties must be reviewed so the framework represents the elements and reasoning pathways in students' knowledge structures.
constraints: The article states that applying the framework to develop assessment and instruction is deferred to follow-up studies.
target_learning_goals: deep conceptual understanding of Newton's third law
examples: The framework's bottom layer lists contextual variables such as mass, size, velocity, and acceleration, and settings such as push, collision, force at a distance, or an object at rest.
